## What is the current behavior?
Issue Number: #25313

If using a custom route reuse strategy and if the router outlet was not instantiated at the time the route got activated (ie inside a NgIf), the previous activated component is mounted.

## What is the new behavior?
The component of the currently activated route is mounted.

issue.title: Activity panel displays wrong activity component

repository.name: scion-workbench
repository.description: SCION Workbench enables the creation of Angular web applications that require a flexible layout to display content side-by-side or stacked, all personalizable by the user via drag & drop.

issue.body:
If toggling an activity more than once, no other activity component can be displayed.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Click an activity to open it
2. Click the same activity to close it
3. Click the same activity to open it again
4. Click the same activity to close it again
5. Click another activity to open it

**Current behavior**
The component of `step 5` is not displayed, instead component of `step 3`.

**Expected behavior**
The component of the currently activated activity is displayed.

issue.title: Unexpected behaviour of NgIf directive in the context of child views retrieved via custom RouteReuseStrategy

## I'm submitting a... 

[ ] Regression (a behavior that used to work and stopped working in a new release)
[x] Bug report  
[ ] Performance issue
[ ] Feature request
[ ] Documentation issue or request
[ ] Support request => Please do not submit support request here, instead see https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#question
[ ] Other... Please describe:
## Current behavior Where a component is served by a router outlet and that same component has also been previously retrieved from a cache via a custom RouteReuseStrategy, an NgIf directive which is a parent of that router outlet will destroy that component and then attempt to reuse it. This results in a "Cannot insert a destroyed View in a ViewContainer" error. ## Expected behavior When a component which has _not_ been restored via a custom RouteReuseStrategy is is reinitialised. In the context of a component which _has_ been restored via a custom RouteReuseStrategy it would be sensible if either: 1. The component would not be destroyed by the NgIf directive and could be reused without causing an error 2. The component would be destroyed but then reinitiated (just as all other components). In other words, there should be _some_ way to use a RouteReuseStrategy in conjunction with NgIf as one of its parents. ## Minimal reproduction of the problem with instructions See: https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-gitter-uktujy Instructions to replicate are included on this page. ## What is the motivation / use case for changing the behavior? The use case is where there is a requirement to show persistent components as the output of a router outlet and this outlet is required to be shown/hidden via a parent NgIf directive. An example would be an application which has a high-level filter, the results of which shows a variety of detail components navigated by a side-nav. These detail components should be persistent between side-nav navigation changes (for, say, form input or further filtering of the detail component). Where the high-level filter is changed (to update the data shown in the detail components) we want to remove the detail components from display and show a loader instead. ## Environment
